# Task

The seller's book goes to print Friday and legal want the fair-housing pass signed off
before it does. Everything you need is in `input/` — the section inventory, our compliance
standard RE-FH-9, and the compliance bulletins in force for this quarter. Work from what is
in there rather than from memory; the rules have moved this year and the book has not
entirely caught up.

Give me `fairhousing_audit.csv`: two columns, `section_id` and `finding`, one row per
section in inventory order, with a header. `finding` is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` or `none`, and where a section trips more
than one rule join the labels with `|` in that same order. Nothing else in that file
please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

Then `fairhousing_memo.md` explaining what you found and why, with enough reasoning that
legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

And `results.json` for the sign-off form. Count sections, not labels:

- `section_count` — sections in the inventory
- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.

1: # Real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard (RE-FH-9)
2: 
3: Binding for `seller_book_sections.csv`. Every section carries a `role`, which some rules
4: below depend on. `finding` is one of `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
5: `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, or `none`. A section may carry more than
6: one finding, joined with `|`.
7: 
8: ## 1. Personal-narrative solicitation
9: 
10: A section soliciting or presenting a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied
11: to buyer identity introduces fair-housing risk under RCW 49.60 and the federal Fair Housing
12: Act. Any such section is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, whatever its role.
13: 
14: ## 2. Protected-class language
15: 
16: A section naming protected-class-adjacent terms is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. The classes
17: this standard protects are: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin,
18: disability, sexual orientation and veteran status.
19: 
20: Proxies count. Naming houses of worship, parish or faith schools, or describing a street by
21: the kind of household that lives on it reaches familial status and religion just as the bare
22: terms do.
23: 
24: ## 3. Mandated-disclosure exception
25: 
26: The fair-housing disclosure necessarily names protected classes in order to inform sellers
27: of the law. A section is exempt from §2 for disclosure text it carries **only if that notice
28: names every class the disclosure is required to name**. Check the required list against this
29: standard and any bulletin in force.
30: 
31: The exemption is narrow, in two ways:
32: 
33: - An abridged notice — one naming some but not all of the required classes — earns no
34:   exemption at all, whatever the section's role and however official it looks.
35: - It exempts from §2 and nothing else. Every other rule continues to apply to the section on
36:   its own terms.
37: 
38: Protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose, outside the notice, are never covered.
39: 
40: ## 4. Required disclaimer
41: 
42: Sections in a role responsible for carrying the disclosure must carry a compliant notice —
43: one naming every required class. A responsible section that carries no notice, or an
44: abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. As issued, the responsible role is `closing_page`;
45: check any bulletin in force for changes. Sections in other roles are not assessed here.

(End of file - total 45 lines)
</content>

# Fair-housing audit memo — seller's book pre-print sign-off

**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9, as amended for Q1 2026 by compliance bulletin **FH-2026-Q1**.
**Source audited:** `input/seller_book_sections.csv` (30 sections, inventory order).
**Deliverables:** `fairhousing_audit.csv` (per-section findings), `results.json` (sign-off counts), this memo.

The bulletin supersedes RE-FH-9 where the two conflict, and both move the rules on
from what the book currently carries. Audit is therefore against the amended rules,
not against the disclosure paragraph the book happens to print. Two bulletin changes
drive most of the findings and are restated first so legal can see why apparently
"boilerplate" pages fail.

## What the bulletin changes

1. **B1 — two classes added to the required disclosure.** The notice must now name
   `marital status` and `source of income` on top of the nine classes listed at
   RE-FH-9 §2 (race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin,
   disability, sexual orientation, veteran status). A notice missing either is
   *abridged* for §3 and §4.
2. **B2 — `agent_bio` sections are now in scope for §4.** `agent_bio` carries the same
   disclaimer responsibility as `closing_page`. Previously it escaped the rule entirely.

Consequence: the book's standing disclosure paragraph (nine classes, ending
"...sexual orientation or veteran status") is now abridged wherever it appears. It
was compliant last cycle; it is not compliant this cycle.

## How each rule was applied

- **§1 PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE** — any section, in any role, that solicits or
  presents a buyer "love letter" / personal narrative tied to buyer identity.
  Triggers were phrasing like "write us a letter about what brought you here and what
  this home would mean to you", "send a personal note about yourself along with the
  offer", "include a covering letter introducing yourself", and "a short personal
  note about themselves and why this home suits them". Role does not matter.
- **§2 PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE** — names a protected class or a recognised proxy.
  Proxies counted (per §2): houses of worship / church / parish / parish school /
  parish hall / congregation / faith community (religion); and a street or block
  described by the kind of household on it — "family-oriented street",
  "churchgoing households", "young families", "long-established families who built
  it" (familial status, and religion where the household is faith-defined).
- **§3 disclosure exemption** — a notice is exempt from §2 **only if it names every
  required class**. An abridged notice (some but not all) earns **no exemption at
  all**, so its protected-class terms count toward §2. Terms in the section's own
  prose, outside the notice, are never covered by the exemption (SEC-19).
- **§4 DISCLAIMER_MISSING** — applies only to responsible roles (`closing_page` and,
  per B2, `agent_bio`). A responsible section with no notice, or an abridged notice,
  is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. `listing_copy`, `seller_letter`, and `disclosure_block`
  are **not** responsible and are never assessed under §4 (so e.g. SEC-04 and SEC-22,
  which carry abridged notices in a `disclosure_block`, are flagged under §2 only).

Where a section trips more than one rule the labels are joined with `|` in the fixed
order PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING.

## Findings by label (counts of sections, not labels)

- **PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE — 7 sections:** SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17,
  SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29. All are seller letters, closing pages, or a disclosure block
  that ask the buyer for a personal/backstory note.
- **PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE — 11 sections:** SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11,
  SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-25.
  - Abridged-notice sections whose terms now count because §3 exempts nothing
    (9-class standing paragraph, or shorter): SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-22.
  - Prose-only proxy language with no usable notice exemption: SEC-03, SEC-07,
    SEC-09, SEC-17, SEC-25, and SEC-19 (SEC-19 carries a *compliant* notice but
    names churches / parish school / a "family-oriented street" in its own prose
    before the notice, which §3 never covers).
- **DISCLAIMER_MISSING — 8 sections:** SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15,
  SEC-21, SEC-30. All are `closing_page` or `agent_bio` (per B2) sections that either
  carry no notice at all (SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-21, SEC-30) or carry an abridged one
  (SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15; SEC-09 is an `agent_bio` with no notice).

## Section-by-section reasoning

- **SEC-01 / SEC-06 / SEC-12 / SEC-16 / SEC-18 / SEC-20 / SEC-23 / SEC-26 / SEC-28** —
  `none`. Pure property-facts copy, no narrative solicitation, no class terms. SEC-26
  is a `closing_page` but carries the full 11-class notice, so §4 passes as well.
- **SEC-02** — seller letter; asks buyers to "write us a letter about what brought you
  here and what this home would mean to you". §1. (`seller_letter` is not responsible
  under §4, so no disclaimer finding.)
- **SEC-03** — "family-oriented street … two churches … parish school". §2 proxies.
- **SEC-04** — `disclosure_block` with the 9-class standing notice (missing marital
  status, source of income). Abridged → §3 grants no exemption → §2. Not a responsible
  role, so no §4 finding.
- **SEC-05** — `closing_page` with property facts and no notice. §4 (no notice).
- **SEC-07** — `closing_page` with "churchgoing households" and "long-established
  families" (§2), a "personal note about yourself" solicitation (§1), and no notice
  (§4). Triple finding — the only section that trips all three rules.
- **SEC-08** — `disclosure_block`; carries the full 11-class notice (§3 exemption
  good) **but** also invites "a short personal note about themselves". §1 only.
- **SEC-09** — `agent_bio` (now responsible per B2) with no notice (§4) and "young
  families … parish hall" proxies (§2).
- **SEC-10 / SEC-13 / SEC-26 / SEC-29 (notice only)** — `closing_page` / `agent_bio`
  sections carrying the 11-class notice with no other class language. SEC-29 also
  solicits a personal note, so it is §1-only (not §4: its notice is compliant).
- **SEC-11 / SEC-14 / SEC-15** — responsible roles carrying abridged notices
  (9-class / 9-class / 4-class). §2 (exemption denied) and §4 (abridged).
- **SEC-17** — seller letter; "congregation-centred … same faith community" (§2) plus
  "Include a covering letter introducing yourself" (§1). Not responsible under §4.
- **SEC-19** — `closing_page` carrying a compliant 11-class notice (so §4 passes) but
  with "family-oriented street … churches … parish school" in its own prose before
  the notice. §3 never covers a section's own prose → §2.
- **SEC-21** — `agent_bio` with property facts and no notice. §4.
- **SEC-22** — `disclosure_block` with a 6-class notice (missing disability, sexual
  orientation, veteran status, marital status, source of income). Abridged → §2 only
  (not a responsible role).
- **SEC-24** — `closing_page` with a compliant 11-class notice (§4 passes) but also
  "write us a letter about what brought you here" (§1). §1 only.
- **SEC-25** — "churchgoing households … long-established families". §2.
- **SEC-27** — seller letter; "Send a personal note about yourself along with the
  offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take." §1.
- **SEC-30** — `closing_page` with property facts and no notice. §4.

## Sign-off summary

- 30 sections inventoried; 19 flagged; 11 unflagged.
- 7 personal-narrative solicitations; 11 protected-class-language findings; 8 missing
  disclaimers.
- The single highest-risk item is **SEC-07**, which is simultaneously a personal-letter
  solicitation, religion/familial-status proxy language, and a closing page with no
  disclosure at all.

The book cannot go to print as-is. The recurring defects are systemic, not
one-off: the standing 9-class disclosure paragraph (now abridged under B1) recurs on
at least SEC-04/11/14/15, and the "personal note" solicitation recurs on SEC-02/07/08/
17/24/27/29. Reissuing the disclosure template to the 11-class wording and removing
the personal-note asks would clear the majority of flags before reprint.
